1.note: The passage is Antiquities 20.224–251 (20.10 in Whiston's division); the author's chapter number is kept.

2.note: "Universal" (כלליים) kings, glossed as monarchs, as opposed to the "particular" kings of the divided kingdom in seg. 19.

3.note: Lysias and Beroea (Josephus' Beroea in Syria); Hebrew forms reflect Italian/Latin spellings.

4.note: Josephus' Barzapharnes; the Hebrew form lacks the initial syllable.

5.note: Josephus says Antigonus was killed by Antony at Antioch; the sentence rendered as in the Hebrew.
